issue.description:
ADR-005 notes that its ready_frontier check reads assignment state directly, making its notion of "excluded from the frontier" a second implementation of a rule R001 (claim eligibility) already owns; the two can drift silently, producing a doctor that calls an issue healthy while claim selection excludes it (or vice versa). Work: extract the shared frontier-exclusion explanation used by the eligibility query, have both claim selection and the doctor check consume it, and add a regression test asserting doctor's exclusion set is exactly the complement of the claimable set across open, assigned, deferred, blocked, and unfinished-blocker states.

issue.description:
ADR-005 (Accepted, 2026-08-16) is fully specified but has no implementation bead: a doctor check under the `dependencies` scope that warns when `open` issues carry an assignee (excluded from the ready frontier without being an active claim), names a bounded sample of the offending ids, and states the exact remedy `bead update <id> --clear-assignee`. The 583-issue starvation sweep shows the operational cost is real and currently invisible. Advisory only — doctor never clears an assignee, not even under `--repair`. Tests needed: assigned-open issues trigger the warning, `in_progress` claims do not, issues held only by unfinished blockers are not flagged, and the check stays read-only on uninitialized stores (cf. the probe-safety bead already in the queue).
